The hoverboard uses magnetic levitation with liquid nitrogen-cooled superconductors and permanent magnets to give the hoverboard "frictionless movement" of a kind that had been thought impossible, according to Lexus.

For any non science people this means the hoverboard is really just a mock-up.

They took super conducting magnets (which only work below maybe 200K) and attached them to the bottom of a board. They then put it on top of a special ferromagnetic track so that it would levitate. This will only work on a ferromagnetic track, it will not hover over: water, asphalt, grass, cement, wood, plastic, etc.

Also it relies on the board's magnets being super cooled below 200K (-100 F or -73C). So good luck using it on a hot summer day in southern California or even Antartica.
